knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Scalping a stressed lawn or setting the lowest height removes too much leaf and weakens the turf. Raising the height and lowering it gradually, with stress signs recorded, is the correct approach.
A sharp blade cuts cleanly. A blunt blade tears the leaf, leaving brown edges and extra stress.
Mowing up and down a slope can tip the machine. The safe method is across the face where stable, and stopping when the machine is unsafe.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied mock lawn card with a species description, the learner names the most likely turf type or records the uncertainty, and states the height they would set and why, within the assessor's set time.
The learner walks a supplied mock lawn, identifies at least two signs of stress from a supplied list, and records them on the job sheet.
The learner completes a pre-mow check on a supplied mock mowing zone, removing the simulated hazards before the mower starts.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed species and height record for the mock lawn, signed by the assessor.
Assessor observation record of the stress-sign walk.
Pre-mow hazard check record for the mock zone.
stopWorkCriteria: Mowing the simulated zone with a person or pet inside it.
Mowing up and down the simulated slope with the mower the assessor has identified as unstable.
Clearing a simulated blockage without switching off the mower.
